findings.summary: the runs view reports failed receipts as delivered
findings.text: `delivered` hands back worker_inbox.receipts() unfiltered, and the same commit made that list carry failure receipts (worker_inbox.py:212 adds a `failed` key). A message the hook could not read therefore appears under a key the view, its docstring at mcp_views.py:4325 and the commit message all call delivered, which contradicts the rule this commit states — a failed receipt is not a delivery — and the manifest finding at worker_inbox.py:338 already filters the same list for that reason. A reader counting `delivered` overstates what reached the worker.

findings.summary: a broadly swallowed OSError hides a queued message from the view with no record
findings.text: `_unclaimed_message` swallows every OSError, not the FileNotFoundError its docstring describes. A waiting message that cannot be read for any other reason (a vanished run directory, a vanished message, an I/O or name error on GPFS) is dropped from the answer with no receipt and no count, so the view reports an empty inbox while a message is still queued — the silent loss the sibling repair in this same commit exists to prevent. Catching FileNotFoundError alone, or surfacing any other OSError in the entry, would keep the race tolerated and the real failure visible.

findings.summary: the mid-read claim is asserted but the receipt the docstring promises is not
findings.text: The docstring states the delivered message's receipt appears in the same answer, but the case at tests/test_worker_inbox.py:395-396 asserts only that `unclaimed` is empty and `unclaimed_count` is zero. An implementation returning no `delivered` key at all, or an empty one, would pass, so the half of the claim that explains why the race is harmless is unguarded; asserting view["inbox"]["delivered"][0]["message"] would make the docstring and the test agree.
